data.description:
Adds the create-bug dialogue prompt for human filers. When the bug being filed will carry the CLI_user tag, the dialogue asks the filer to select one of the seven detected_by values and applies the resulting tag. Also updates create-bug SKILL.md and bug-report-template.md to document the field, its allowed values, and when it is required vs auto-set. Builds on the infer-detected-by.sh story's tag vocabulary (the dialogue may reuse the helper's allowed-values constant).

## Done Definitions

- Filing a CLI_user-tagged bug via /dso:create-bug prompts the filer to select one of the seven detected_by values before ticket creation completes ← Satisfies: sc-1
- The resulting bug ticket carries a detected_by:<chosen-channel> tag matching the filer's selection ← Satisfies: sc-1
- create-bug SKILL.md documents the detected_by field, the seven allowed values, when it is required (CLI_user-tagged bugs) vs auto-set (agent paths), and the default ('other'); the seven allowed values (tests, review-llm, review-human, production, user-report, internal-dogfood, other) are listed verbatim in the document ← Satisfies: sc-2
- bug-report-template.md documents the detected_by field and its allowed values; the seven allowed values (tests, review-llm, review-human, production, user-report, internal-dogfood, other) are listed verbatim in the document ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Integration test exercises the CLI_user dialogue path end-to-end and asserts the resulting ticket carries a detected_by tag from the allowed set ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [UX] The dialogue prompt should display the seven values with one-line descriptions so the filer can pick the right channel without leaving the dialogue.
- [Reliability] Reject filer input that is not one of the seven values rather than silently defaulting — silent default would mask a schema gap (one of the surviving Red/Blue scenarios).

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked
data.title: As a human filer using /dso:create-bug, I want the dialogue to prompt me for detected_by when my bug is CLI_user-tagged, so that human-filed bugs carry channel attribution.
